# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

**How I checked it:** the program seeds its random numbers from the current time. So I ran both programs side by side in pseudo-terminals, started in the same second, and compared their raw output. They matched for:
- every flag and many combinations of them
- all the in-program keys, including pause with `p`/`P`
- Ctrl-C, Ctrl-\ and Ctrl-Z, with and without lock mode (`-L`)
- the terminal types xterm, screen, tmux-256color, linux, vt100 and ansi, in both the plain C and UTF-8 locales
- terminal sizes from 1×1 up to 50×200, including repeated window resizes
- the help, version and error output, with exit codes
- screen captures taken in tmux

**Quirks of the original that I copied on purpose:**
- **Linking:** it uses the wide-character curses library and sets the locale at startup. `-c` draws half-width katakana (U+FF66–U+FF9D), and the leading white characters are drawn differently from the rest.
- **Exit codes:** an invalid `-C` colour prints its error to stderr but exits with status 0. An unknown option prints the usage and also exits 0. `-l` always fails with "Unable to use both \"setfont\" and \"consolechars\"" and exits 0.
- **`-n` bug:** `-n` turns the leading white characters bold, which is the opposite of what it says.
- **Black key:** the README says `)` switches to black, but the original has no `)` key, so mine doesn't either.
- **Resizing:** the drawing area keeps its original size; only the internal grid is rebuilt. The `-M` message is drawn once after all the columns. These only show up in output after a resize, and both matched.
- **Crashes:** `-f` with no `TERM` set segfaults. A 3-row terminal crashes with a divide-by-zero.
- **Version line:** the original prints its own build time ("compiled 22:13:51, Jun 11 2026"), so I hard-coded that text.

**Build:** `compile.sh` checks for a C compiler and the wide-character curses headers, and tries to install them with the system package manager if they're missing. It then builds `./executable`. It deletes any existing `./executable` first, which means running it in the workspace replaces the original binary. I tested it in a fresh clone instead, so the original is still in place, untracked and covered by `.gitignore`.

I rewrote the program from scratch in C, in `src/cmatrix.c`. When both are started in the same second, mine produces byte-for-byte the same terminal output as the original in every case I tested. The work is committed. `compile.sh` builds `./executable` from a fresh clone; I ran it in `/tmp/fresh` and the result matched the original too.

**How I checked it:** the original seeds its random numbers from the clock, so two copies started in the same second draw the same rain. I wrote a small harness that runs both in pseudo-terminals at the same moment and compares the raw output. Everything below matched exactly, or one output was a prefix of the other because the run was cut off at a different point:
- **Options:** every display option and combination, including all `-C` colours and `-u 0` to `9`.
- **Terminals and locales:** several terminal types (xterm, screen, tmux, linux, vt100, ansi) in both the plain C locale and UTF-8.
- **Sizes:** screens from 1×1 up to 200 columns. At exactly 3 rows both crash with the same divide-by-zero.
- **Keys:** every interactive key and key sequence, including lock mode ignoring `q`.
- **Signals:** Ctrl-C, Ctrl-\, Ctrl-Z, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, and repeated window resizes.
- **Exit paths:** help, version and error output with their exit codes, the console-font error from `-l`, `-t`, screensaver mode (it pushes your keystroke back to the shell, as the original does), and side-by-side `tmux` sessions.

**Behaviours that differ from the README but match the binary:**
- It uses the wide-character ncurses library. `-c` draws half-width katakana (U+FF66 to U+FF9D).
- The version line is hardcoded as `compiled 22:13:51, Jun 11 2026` to match, rather than using my build time.
- An invalid `-C` colour prints its message to stderr and exits with status 0.
- `-n` actually makes the white leading characters bold.
- `-f` crashes if `TERM` is unset.
- There is no `)` key for black. `p`/`P` pause.
- On resize only the rain grid changes size; the screen itself is not resized, and the message box is drawn once after all the columns.

**Building:** `compile.sh` installs a compiler and ncurses headers with the system package manager only if they are missing. It deletes any existing `./executable` before linking, so running it in `/workspace` will replace the original binary. `.gitignore` excludes `/executable` and other build output, and the original binary is still in place, untracked.
